item.title: Give Every Agent Its Own Room
item.description: Apple silicon Macs are quiet enough to run a local model all day. The agent connected to that model is a different story: it needs a shell, a filesystem, and a network, and if those have no boundary they are your shell, your filesystem, and your network. Koala is an experiment in giving every agent its own Linux VM, with network policy and credentials staying on the Mac host.

item.title: Give the Agent a Desk, Not Your Keys
item.description: You would never give a new hire root on the machine holding your keys. Kagebox is an experiment in giving an autonomous agent a whole machine that is not yours: its own kernel, credentials that stay host side, a latch it cannot reach, and a spend cap. Every layer of it can fail open without saying so, and that turned out to be the lesson.
